rows.text: Over the tannery in Muddlecombe lived a small goblin with nobody at all.
Then, one rainy night, somebody knocked.
Delivery for the grandchild of Bartleby Snatchwick. Sign here. Or bite here. I hear you're a biter.
Your grandfather, the legendary Lucky Snatchwick, has died inside Mount Grumblegut.
He left you everything. Unfortunately, everything is still in the mountain.
Up Kettle Hill, in the Grumble's shadow, Nib walks you home.
Here we are, Sprout. Wipe your feet. He never did.
The Last Will & Considerable Testament of Bartleby Snatchwick, Esq.
I, Bartleby "Lucky" Snatchwick, being of sound mind and even sounder luck, do hereby leave EVERYTHING to my grandchild, whom I met only once. You bit me. Good instincts.
Everything is presently inside Mount Grumblegut, in the pockets of assorted monsters who picked it up after I fell over. Each piece is engraved with my name. They know it is not theirs.
Bring my things home and set them in the Snatchwick Cabinet of Considerable Curiosities. Only what you are holding when you get out counts. What the mountain keeps, it keeps.
When the Cabinet is full, this cabin and the deed to Kettle Hill are yours. Nib will stamp it. Nib loves stamping.
Nib is to be paid in biscuits. Do not open the left-hand drawer of my desk.

rows.where: Bubble over Nib while the tutorial is not done

rows.text: Welcome home, Sprout. Well. His home. Yours on paper, once the cabinet's full.
Everything with his name on it went into the mountain with him. The monsters have been wearing it ever since.
Bring it back, put it on his shelves, and the deed's yours. I'll stamp it. I love stamping.

rows.where: Run door clicked before the tutorial is done
rows.text: Whoa, whoa. Straight into the Grumble? Without a word from the professional?
First delve's on me. I'll walk you through it. What do you say?
Just like him. Off you go. Try to come back with more than you left with.

rows.where: After the tutorial finishes, back in the cabin
rows.text: There. Practically a professional. Now go and fetch his things.
He used to sit in that chair and flip a coin for hours. Never lost a toss. Never explained it.
The map's wrong, by the way. He drew it from memory. His memory was mostly confidence.
If the radio stops, tap the glass. Gently. Gloria bites.
Every piece is engraved: 'Property of B. Snatchwick. If found, how dare you.'
He tied rope ladders in every belly of the mountain. 'For emergencies.' He used them for lunch.
I'm not sentimental. I'm an executor. Executors don't cry. They file.
That's him, the year he lost a duel to a hatstand. He'd want me to say 'won'.
Keep it lit. He said the cabin gets lonely.

rows.where: Click the hero in the chair
rows.text: His chair. Rocks on its own sometimes. Draughts. Definitely draughts.

rows.where: Homecoming that crosses 25% of the cabinet
rows.text: A quarter of his shelves! He'd have thrown a party. Then knocked something over at it.

rows.where: Homecoming that crosses 50% of the cabinet
rows.text: Halfway, Sprout. The cabin's starting to smell like him again. That's a compliment. Mostly.

rows.where: Homecoming that crosses 75% of the cabinet
rows.text: Three quarters. I've started drafting the deed. In pencil. I'm not made of ink.
Empty? Well. You came back. That's the part he never managed.
The mountain keeps what it catches. You'll catch it back.
Sit. Warm up. The Grumble isn't going anywhere. It's a mountain.
Look at that! Home where it belongs!
He'd be insufferable about this. In a good way.

rows.where: First NEW item flies to the hall
rows.text: That one's new! Off to the hall with it.

rows.where: Win homecoming with no new items
rows.text: Nothing new, but a good haul's a good haul. His things like being held.
Found them! Behind the biscuits. Where else?
Four keys, four doors. Let's see what he was hiding.

rows.text: Give up? The sack comes home empty.
Every shelf full. Every curiosity home.
"By the powers vested in me by a dead goblin and a rubber stamp..."
"...the cabin on Kettle Hill belongs to his grandchild."
Grandpa's luck, it turns out, runs in the family.
He'd have liked you, Sprout. He'd never have said so. He'd have put it in a footnote.
